title: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the …
body: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the edited bullet exits non-zero]) is structurally vacuous: line 901 contains zero path tokens, so the loop body never executes and the oracle passes with zero iterations. The intent (no gitignored path token in the bullet) is satisfied, but a zero-match sweep passing silently is the same self-nullifying shape the bullet at patterns.md:901 warns about. Consider asserting a non-zero token count before iterating.

title: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` …
body: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` and `$c:s` are path modifiers, so a loop written as `git show "$c:test/foo.ts"` silently expands to `<sha>est/foo.ts` and, with stderr redirected, yields an empty file and a bogus `grep -c` of 0 for every commit. This produced two wrong measurements during this review and is the unidentified cause of the 'for-loop pipeline gave inconsistent readings' note in the round-2 artifact. Per-commit sweeps should run under an explicit `bash -c`.

title: The stderr-capture assertions were moved inside the withFakeClock callback (Sit…
body: The stderr-capture assertions were moved inside the withFakeClock callback (Site A lines ~341-343, Site B AC4 ~line 745), so they execute while process.stderr.write is still patched. On assertion failure the framework's diff output routes into the captured chunks rather than the real terminal, which can obscure failure diagnostics. Consider exposing the captured chunks after the helper returns (or asserting outside the callback) so failures print normally. Non-blocking: restore is guaranteed by the finally, and all tests pass.

This mirrors the existing writeSessionStartFn placement and matches the spec, so it is not a defect; a future note could clarify whether the container path wants its own liveness marker.

title: runPause always returns 0 even if setPause silently swallowed a write failure (…

Consider having setPause surface a best-effort boolean so pause can warn (not fail) when the marker could not be written. (Carried from review round 1; non-blocking.)

Writing the JSON line first, then emitting the event, keeps the primary contract independent of the audit side effect.

title: The module header justifies positive-signal-only detection by saying a future b…

The real repo-wide guard is the new US-003 compiled integration test (which fails loudly in CI on a prefix change); the comment would be more accurate naming that pin instead of a fallback the forkMonitor path does not have.

title: `"$(cat -- 'path')"` fails open: a missing or unreadable prompt file yields an …
body: `"$(cat -- 'path')"` fails open: a missing or unreadable prompt file yields an empty string and claude launches promptless (CAM-41: dies instantly) while runVerifiedDispatch still reports ok. The concrete trigger is the pipe-pane-exited branch (verified-dispatch.ts:172-176), where respawn-pane has already succeeded and the worker shell is starting when runVerifiedWorkerDispatch deletes that dispatch's prompt file, racing the pane shell's cat. The residual is a misdiagnosed terminal (pane-died instead of prompt-read-failed) rather than true silence, since the marker/event/notify still fire on that path, which is why this stays a SUGGESTION. Making the read fail loudly (so an absent prompt becomes an explicit pane death) would close the last fail-open in a PRD whose thesis is that no dispatch fails silently.

The result-kind conflation is pre-existing on main; this change propagates it into the new durable marker and the live notification, where a wrong cause is more visible.

Recording the provenance would be the strongest available evidence that ADR-0049's reserve-list practice paid for itself, which is a fact a future naming cycle would want on the record. (Closely related to the line-13 WARNING; likely fixed in the same edit.)

title: The prowmark runner-up entry records its eliminatory reason correctly (Promark,…
body: The prowmark runner-up entry records its eliminatory reason correctly (Promark, D'Addario, 1957) but flattens its recorded merit to 'a clean namespace sweep'. CAM-434 spec.gotchas is more specific and more decision-relevant: prowmark 'era o unico com WHOIS no match em todos os TLDs, portanto o unico onde seriamos donos de .com e .dev e .io e .app'. That matters because ADR-0050:47 separately books gateship.com as a knowingly 'accepted cost'; a reader cannot presently see that the runner-up was the one candidate that would have delivered the .com the adopted name lacks. Not an AC5 violation (AC5 asks for the eliminatory reason, which is present and correct), but it is the trade-off half of the record.

title: Re-raised from round 2: the gate's positive-evidence marker (RAN_LINE_RE, 'Ran …
body: Re-raised from round 2: the gate's positive-evidence marker (RAN_LINE_RE, 'Ran N tests across M files.') and its pass/skip line parsers depend on Bun's stdout summary FORMAT. Reviewer re-confirmed against the official docs this round (https://bun.com/docs/cli/test): the docs guarantee only the exit code ('If a test fails, the test runner exits with a non-zero exit code'), show the summary lines solely inside an example, and never state the skip line is omitted at zero, while documenting --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile as the machine-readable channel. Verified empirically against the local toolchain (bun 1.3.13), so not a defect today, but a Bun formatting change would silently turn the completion check into a permanent red.

The invalid shapes (empty acceptanceCriteria array, blank scope) and the --fast-track flag are covered at the unit layer (test/issue-file.test.ts:857-925), so the behavior itself is tested and this is not a coverage hole, but the end-to-end exit-code plus machine-line contract is proven for only one combination. Carried forward unaddressed from review round 1; noting it only so the drift stays deliberate rather than accidental.

title: The ADR-0040 pin 'AC4: exhausting re-plan rounds on a persistently-broken oracl…

It passes only because both constants happen to be 2; changing MAX_LINT_REPLAN_ROUNDS alone would fail this pin for the wrong reason. The PRD required the pin stay UNMODIFIED, so this was correctly left alone in this PR, but the constant reference is now semantically wrong and worth re-pointing in a follow-up.

title: The invariant that keeps a new union member away from the cast is still not com…

The artifact currently contains only 'ci-gated', so there is no live defect, and the values originate from cam's own emit site; a membership check against the two literals would make the narrowing sound rather than asserted.
